record.prompt_text:
### Exercise 15.6: Recognise pairs of angles between parallel lines

3. In the diagram below, $RS \parallel TO$ and $MN$ is a transversal.

Source image: https://electricbookworks.github.io/siyavula-open-textbooks-images/items/images/web/ebw-jss1-15-031.png

What type of angle pair is shown by the shaded angles?

What is the relationship between the two angles?
record.answer_text:
If we highlight the angles we will see an "N" shape.

Highlighted image: https://electricbookworks.github.io/siyavula-open-textbooks-images/items/images/web/ebw-jss1-15-032.png

The shaded angles are alternate angles.

The alternate angles are equal because $RS \parallel TO$.

closest_candidate_atomic_objectives.rationale: The textbook explicitly teaches co-interior angles alongside corresponding and alternate angles, and includes an exercise item for recognising them. The canonical curriculum list names alternate and corresponding angles but omits co-interior angles.

closest_candidate_atomic_objectives.proposed_objective_text: Apply angle relationships in real-world contexts.
closest_candidate_atomic_objectives.evidence_quote: we can apply our knowledge in real life.
closest_candidate_atomic_objectives.rationale: The practical-application records ask learners to use angle relationships in map, painting, and contextual diagrams. They depend on the existing angle relationships but express a distinct application objective.
